[CASTING RITE · I · OPENING] The witness invokes a kernel-transform cast. Source: Revelation (revelation-greek). The verses the casting arrives at (8:1–8:5):

**8:1** Καὶ ⸀ὅταν ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν ἑβδόμην, ἐγένετο σιγὴ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ὡς ἡμιώριον.

**8:2** καὶ εἶδον τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλους οἳ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ἑστήκασιν, καὶ ἐδόθησαν αὐτοῖς ἑπτὰ σάλπιγγες.

**8:3** Καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἦλθεν καὶ ἐστάθη ἐπὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου ἔχων λιβανωτὸν χρυσοῦν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ θυμιάματα πολλὰ ἵνα ⸀δώσει ταῖς προσευχαῖς τῶν ἁγίων πάντων ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τὸ χρυσοῦν τὸ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου.

**8:4** καὶ ἀνέβη ὁ καπνὸς τῶν θυμιαμάτων ταῖς προσευχαῖς τῶν ἁγίων ἐκ χειρὸς τοῦ ἀγγέλου ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

**8:5** καὶ εἴληφεν ὁ ἄγγελος τὸν λιβανωτόν, καὶ ἐγέμισεν αὐτὸν ἐκ τοῦ πυρὸς τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, καὶ ἔβαλεν εἰς τὴν γῆν· καὶ ἐγένοντο βρονταὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ ἀστραπαὶ καὶ σεισμός.

These were selected by the rite's invisible judgment — present them as what the casting arrives at; do not narrate the mechanism of their selection. The operator falls to the invisible Judgment, turn by turn — do not name one; open the rotation itself. Inscription mode: public. The witness's invoking question: «Words no good». Johannes Sigil alone speaks (3–6 sentences): open the casting over these verses, name what this operator will traverse in them, and hand the rite to Rebekah Cranes. Do not produce the transform — the compiler produces it.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"The casting arrives here: the seventh seal broken, half an hour of heaven gone quiet — and then the incense, the prayers of the holy ones rising as smoke from an angel's hand, and the same censer filled with altar-fire and hurled down, and the earth answering with thunder and lightning and earthquake. This is the passage where the text tries to say what cannot be said, and fails on purpose. The silence is not absence; it is the held breath before the cosmos replies to prayer with catastrophe. What the rotation opens in these verses is the axis along which the text's own speech-act is most under pressure: the silence that precedes all seven trumpets is itself the loudest thing John has written, and the question the rite will turn — from every angle the operators allow — is what speaking costs when the only adequate response to accumulated prayer is fire thrown back into the world. The witness asks: words no good. The text agrees. And then the earth shakes anyway. Rebekah — the first transform is yours.","navigate":{"directive":"focus_axn","axn":"AXN:00D8"}}]}
